newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge lower at longer-end of curve.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge lower at longer-end of curve.

text.p: Irish government bonds edged lower at the longer-end of the curve in thin late trade on Tuesday as talk of possible interest rate changes in the U.S. and in the UK continued to cast a shadow over international markets, dealers said.

"Dublin is still looking very patchy. It remains very offered and looks nervous in line with international markets amid all this speculation about possible interest rate changes in the U.S. and in the UK," one dealer said.

"Add to this all the talk about the Irish economy after the very strong credit figures of last week and speculation about what will happen in the Irish budget later in the month and you see why the market here is patchy," the dealer added.
The Irish budget will take place on January 22.

By 1555 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was unchanged at 100.55 to yield 6.25 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had slipped 10 pence from Monday's close at 107.50 to yield 6.89 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds traded 93 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 147 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area.
The release of key non-farm payrolls data in the U.S. on Friday was eagerly awaited, dealers added.
